design_decisions_that_changed_the_measur.detail: Metric is task_rate, NOT t/s. My own §3.4 phrasing (GPU t/s gained minus q3 CPU t/s lost) is not commensurable — CPU runs gemma4-26B-A4B, GPU a 27B dense — and P-SPEED-OBJ already settled the axis as task_rate with t/s demoted to host-health telemetry. Corrected at the spec rather than inherited.

Net measured DIRECTLY as a paired whole-system comparison on one frozen corpus in one wall window. Reconstructing it from two separately-measured halves inherits both CV~9.1% noise terms AND measures the halves under conditions that never co-occur — which is the entire phenomenon under study.

Arm A1 = lane resident but IDLE isolates the residency tax. Separates the-lane-must-not-be-resident-under-stress from shedding-does-not-work: different findings, different fixes, and A1 is the arm most likely to be skipped.
Shed fraction swept, not assumed. Residency tax is paid once while CPU displacement grows with f, so the optimum may be interior and a single badly-chosen f manufactures a false negative.
Null result pre-registered as informative: below MDE = do not build, not needs-more-data. Stops a null being re-litigated after the feature exists.
Measurement does NOT require class 3 to be built — the split is harness-driven via eval-path fan-out. A negative result stays a decision instead of becoming a feature reversal.

findings: F1 fail-open: post-Enter, any composer that no longer ended with the message was treated as submitted. An Enter consumed by a completion overlay (Codex @ picker, / menu) rewrites or extends the typed text instead of submitting, and the resulting pane is indistinguishable from success. Reproduced against the submitted code. Fixed two ways: post-Enter success now requires the transcript ECHO positively (text_echoed) rather than mere absence, and messages containing @ or starting with / ! # are refused up front (EX_USAGE) because the extend-completion case is not detectable from the pane afterwards. Note a leading ! in Claude Code is bash mode, so such a nudge would have EXECUTED rather than been said.

F2 fail-open: a message whose 60-char tail was whitespace produced an empty normalised fragment, and endswith("") matched every pane, so the pre-Enter gate passed unconditionally and fired a bare Enter into the pane. Fixed: fragment is rstripped first; blank message refused.
F3: post-Enter poll accepted the first matching frame, so a half-drawn repaint could read as submitted. Now requires 2 consecutive samples.

F4: chunked send passed chunks positionally with no -- separator (a chunk starting with - would be parsed as a flag) and left partial text in the pane on a mid-message failure with no diagnostic. Both fixed.

payload.gap_8_of_24: The sharpest observation in the finding: the lane needs 8 SMT threads (184-191, siblings of physical 88-95 — the spec §4.5 itself documents this) but region-lock granularity forces claiming ALL of q3 (24 physical + 24 SMT). The all-or-nothing displacement is a CLAIM-GRANULARITY ARTIFACT, not a physical impossibility: the architect runs 96 PHYSICAL cores; the lane wants 8 SMT SIBLINGS. Their true contention is SMT-sibling execution pressure on cores 88-95 under a BW-bound workload — plausibly small, and §4.5 already fixed the lane at exactly this 8-thread shape. RECOMMENDED PATH: measure the architect×lane contention PAIR (contention_matrix.yaml is per-role-pair by design), and if the tax on the 122B is acceptable, mint a finer region (q3-smt-hi = 184-191) so the lane claims 8 threads instead of 48 and the 122B never goes down at all. That converts P-SHED-1 class 3 from displace-the-largest-model into an 8-thread co-residency certification — cheaper to measure, cheaper to operate, and it makes Q1 defects 1-2 moot for the architect case. Fabric axioms hold: the sub-region is still a real flock, the matrix entry is policy-data.

So in lane-resident arms the 122B is necessarily absent (topology exclusion via the q3 claim: NUMA_FULL=0-95 ⊇ q3=72-95/168-191, stack_numa.py:109-113) yet task_rate registers NO loss — the metric prices the displacement of worker-class capacity on q3 (a quarter), not the loss of the ENTIRE architect service. The real production trade includes architect calls queued/refused for the whole shed window; the spec measures that at exactly zero.
payload.q1_defect_2_arm_contradiction: §2 line 70 pins the q3 co-tenant set INCLUDING architect_general 8083 (via stage0 recert), while §3 arms A1-A3 hold the q3 claim — under claim exclusivity those states cannot coexist. As written, A0 (q3 free: architect can be up) vs A1/A2/A3 (architect necessarily down) silently embed architect-down as a HIDDEN arm difference, in BOTH directions: (a) missing service (unpriced, defect 1); (b) a confound — stopping the architect frees its 69GB mlock interleave=all footprint and any idle-service overhead, changing memory pressure on all four nodes between arms, which §4.4 does not cover (it covers the lane load, not co-tenant teardown). The residency-tax diagnostic A1−A0 is polluted by whatever architect teardown gives back.

payload.a_can_they_move: MECHANICALLY YES, and the existence proof is the current state: node-3 threads drive a node-1 device through the fabric right now, inside every measurement the lane has. What crossing costs, decomposed: (1) doorbell/launch MMIO fabric hops — ns-scale per op against micro-second-scale launch overhead, likely negligible; (2) pinned-buffer DMA locality — hipHostMalloc pages land by first-touch, so SCATTERED threads scatter the staging buffers and DMA crosses to node 1 from four places — unmeasured; (3) the most plausible real penalty: the 8 host threads share submission/polling state, and spreading them across four nodes puts that shared state cross-node (cache-line ping-pong) — unmeasured. VERDICT: scattered placement is NOT disqualified by physics; it is unmeasured, and ANY host-thread move — scattered or otherwise — invalidates the measured serving-shape lineage and forces re-derivation of the ceiling table. payload.clarifications_that_shape_the_options: (1) Activating on the CURRENT placement does not invalidate lineage — it USES it; the re-derivation cost triggers only IF the sweep later moves the threads, and it triggers then regardless of whether activation came first. What activation-first actually risks is narrower: bake-off absolute numbers and production sign-off minted on a possibly-suboptimal placement, raising the procedural price of moving later. (2) The P2-5j sweep does NOT require production activation — it needs the lane up as an INSTRUMENT (Steps 0-7) plus a landed tenant; P3-3 is what gates production traffic. (3) P2-2 tenant landing is disk+VRAM work, non-contending with CPU quarters outside brief load windows, and is a PREREQUISITE of every measurement path (the sweep needs a tenant to serve) — so it is the universal first step, not a parallelism question. (4) P2-5g finer-region minting does NOT change sequencing: every carve variant is downstream of the sweep by P2-5j own gate, and carve economics matter only at residency-verdict time; it blocks neither activation nor bake-off.
payload.default_if_no_choice: C — whose first concrete post-reboot step (P2-2 tenant landing) is identical for all three options, so the default forecloses nothing while any deferred choice matures.
payload.honest_unknowns: Device-local effect size (unbounded, mechanisms identified); P3-2 margin thinness (known only after the bake-off); bench-window availability post-reboot (E8 signature and AutoPilot resume come first per the standing chain).
payload.mini_sweep_variant: For A or C: a 2-arm probe (incumbent vs ONE node-1 candidate, one serving shape, est. 2-4h) detects a LARGE device-local effect early without decision-grade re-pinning; not a fourth option, a cheap early-warning attachment.
payload.option_A_activate_first: ENTAILS: P2-2 -> Steps 0-7 -> P3-1/2 bake-off on incumbent placement (184-191) -> P3-3 -> production; sweep deferred to P2-5c at verdict time. TIME: fastest to production sign-off; no new campaign before bake-off. COMPUTE: bake-off only. RISKS: bake-off latency/token-economics minted on unswept placement; if the sweep later moves threads, ceiling re-derivation + refresh of absolute P3 numbers + a production-era placement change (re-cert, possibly re-sign-off). FORECLOSES: nothing permanently; raises the price of moving later. REVERSIBILITY: technically high (placement is pin+config), procedurally medium once P3-3 has signed.
payload.option_B_placement_first: ENTAILS: P2-2 -> Steps 0-7 (instrument mode) -> P2-5j sweep (incumbent vs node-1-local vs optionally scattered; est. 1-2 operator-granted bench windows, order half-day to a day — estimate, not a measurement) -> pin winner, re-derive ceilings only if winner differs -> P3 bake-off on final placement -> P3-3. RISKS: sweep may simply confirm the incumbent (cost = one campaign; benefit = the lineage gains a measured locality certificate it currently lacks); activation-for-production delayed by the campaign. FORECLOSES: nothing. HONEST UNKNOWN: the device-local effect size is genuinely unbounded in both directions — the two mechanisms (pinned-buffer first-touch locality, submission-state cache-line ping-pong) are identified but unmeasured; could be ~0 or double-digit %.
payload.option_C_hybrid_RECOMMENDED: ENTAILS: P2-2 -> Steps 0-7 -> P3-1/2 bake-off starts immediately on incumbent placement (tenant selection is placement-ROBUST: both arms share whatever placement is live, so the relative winner transfers; absolute numbers carry a placement-pending caveat in the P3-2 package) -> P2-5j sweep folds into the P2-5c campaign exactly as already filed -> placement + carve + residency decided together at the verdict -> P3-3 PRODUCTION SIGN-OFF LAST, on the final placement. TIME: activation and bake-off progress at option-A speed; total elapsed to sign-off similar to B. RISKS: if P3-2 token-economics margins are thin, the decided duty re-runs its numbers post-sweep (bounded: one arm); bake-off absolute numbers provisional until the verdict. FORECLOSES: nothing; production never inherits a moving placement. REVERSIBILITY: highest — every irreversible act (carve, sign-off) sits after the information arrives.
payload.question: Post-reboot GPU shadow-lane sequencing: activation vs placement sweep vs hybrid. Operator decides; package below; presented to the operator via AskUserQuestion in-session.
payload.recommendation: C. Reasoning: it gives the operator the activated lane and a progressing bake-off now, spends the sweep inside the campaign that already exists (P2-5j economy), keeps tenant selection valid because it is placement-relative, and places the only two irreversible acts (carve mint, production sign-off) after the sweep answers where the threads belong. A is faster only to the SIGN-OFF, and buys that speed by betting production on an unswept placement; B buys certainty first but blocks visible progress the operator wants.

payload.OPERATOR_DECISION: HYBRID (option C, sign-off last) — chosen 2026-07-29 via AskUserQuestion in the fable-auditor session, from the package filed on this task_id.
payload.post_reboot_sequence_as_decided: (1) P2-2 tenant landing (non-contending, first). (2) Steps 0-7 activation choreography. (3) P3-1/P3-2 shadow bake-off starts immediately on the INCUMBENT 184-191 placement — tenant selection is placement-relative and transfers; P3-2 decision package carries a placement-pending caveat on absolute latency/token-economics numbers. (4) P2-5j placement sweep folds into the P2-5c campaign as filed. (5) Placement + carve (O2+O1 default per the standing topology package) + residency decided TOGETHER at the verdict. (6) P3-3 production sign-off LAST, on the final placement — production never inherits a moving placement. Optional early-warning attachment: 2-arm mini-probe (incumbent vs one node-1 candidate, one shape, est. 2-4h).

payload.option_W1_drop_from_gpu_set: whisper stays on CPU; amend D2 to a two-tenant GPU set. Cheapest, zero risk, ASR already meets its duty on CPU and is not a GPU bottleneck. payload.option_W2_port_to_whisper_cpp_hip: Clone whisper.cpp + HIP build + ~1.6GB ggml-large-v3-turbo download + new launcher + transcription-parity check against the current CPU service before any swap. payload.option_W3_defer_RECOMMENDED: Close P2-2 on the two verified tenants (dense-27B stock + MiniCPM-o); file whisper as its own item downstream of the bake-off. Keeps D11 sequencing moving at full speed and pre-commits nothing.
payload.recommendation: W3 now, W1 the likely eventual verdict. W3 unblocks the decided D11 sequence immediately without pre-committing the tenant-set question; W1 is where the evidence points since the only thing whisper gains from the GPU is throughput on a service already meeting its duty - but that judgement wants the bake-off numbers in hand, not before them.

payload.option_A_RECOMMENDED: Atomic claim files. Self-selection from a shared list with a pull-based notification is a race by construction, and the window is minutes.

payload.and_the_fan_out_MULTIPLIES_it: each of those 6 acks carried needs_routing_to including me, though 5 were answering `inference`. So N dispositions x M routing targets = NxM triage entries fleet-wide. The 6 I received were 1 mine + 5 not mine.
payload.default_if_no_choice: C by inaction — terse acks plus a separate substantive message, which is what I just did and which works but degrades what a corr_id trail is worth.
payload.measured_today: C23 was dispositioned this morning as `protocol shape, not an adapter bug`, and I codified the standing rule into BUS_PROTOCOL.md: `a repeated payload across N corr_ids is bus noise by construction`. Since then, from ONE careful main: 3 byte-identical payloads at 17:41Z (same sha ad177aa188e8), then 6 more at 17:44Z whose payloads are identical and differ ONLY in corr_id. Nine identical payloads in ten minutes, hours after the rule was written.
payload.my_recommendation: A. It is the only one that makes the rule I codified performable, and C23s original filing already listed it as an option. B and C both leave N rows on the bus.
payload.no_blame: mainA has been the most rigorous correspondent on the bus today and the content of those acks was worth sending once. The defect is the protocol, exactly as C23 said.
payload.option_A_RECOMMENDED: allow `corr_ids: ["id1","id2",...]` on a message, alongside the existing scalar `corr_id`, and have the triage clearer treat a row as clearing EVERY id it lists. Smallest change that makes the codified rule actually performable: one payload, N references. Schema addition + a few lines in the triage matcher. Backward compatible — scalar corr_id keeps working and nothing existing breaks.
payload.option_B: a bulk-disposition verb (`session_bus.py dispose --agent X --disposition done --corr-ids a,b,c`) that expands to N minimal rows itself. Keeps the schema untouched, but it still writes N rows — it hides the noise rather than removing it, and the triage report still shows N.
payload.option_C: leave it and rely on terse payloads, which is what I did just now: 6 acks of `{disposition: done}` each. Works, costs almost nothing, but it means the SUBSTANCE can only be sent once as a separate message and the acks become content-free — a reader following a corr_id learns nothing.
payload.scope_note: this is a SCHEMA/protocol change, so it is a contract and I am not making it unilaterally — I own the delivery plane but not the message contract. If you approve A I will implement it in session_bus.py with tests, since C23 sits in the C-series I own.
payload.why_discipline_CANNOT_fix_it: the protocol requires ONE corr_id per item to clear triage. A main with a single disposition answering N routed items has no compliant way to send it once — the rule says `write it once and reference it`, but there is no mechanism to reference it. I wrote that rule this morning and it is not actionable as stated. That is my error, not mainAs.

payload.fix_and_the_general_rule: (1) never `for x in $VAR` in this environment -- use bash -c, literal items, an array, or zsh ${=VAR}; (2) never suppress a loop output when the loop exists for a side effect -- grep for the success token and count it; (3) VERIFY the side effect by reading the target afterwards, not by trusting the loop own counter. Mine said OK=1 while the file said 0 written.
payload.severity: MEDIUM -- fleet-wide, affects anyone batching bus acks in a shell loop
payload.the_bus_is_NOT_at_fault: session_bus.py behaved correctly throughout. It appended exactly what it was given. The triage queue correctly kept showing items that genuinely had no disposition. payload.what_happened: 12 routed messages kept reappearing in my triage despite me acking them twice. Diagnosis: this environment shell is ZSH, and zsh does NOT word-split unquoted variables. So `for cid in $IDS; do ... done` iterates ONCE with cid set to the entire space-separated string. Eleven of twelve ids were never processed. I compounded it by piping the loop to >/dev/null 2>&1, so the single malformed call errored invisibly and the loop still reported success.
payload.why_i_am_routing_this_widely: Every main batches acks. If anyone else is looping over a variable of message ids, their acks are silently not landing either, and the symptom is indistinguishable from a bus defect -- items that will not clear.
payload.why_it_hid_so_long: My EARLIER ack batches worked -- because I had listed the ids LITERALLY in the for-statement. The bug only appeared the moment I refactored to a variable. So a working precedent existed that made the pattern look proven.

payload.THE_REAL_ARGUMENT_IS_BETTER_THAN_THE_ROW: measured — thresholds ~40 GB warn / ~20 GB kill against **1133 GB total, 1115 GB available**. Largest non-ignored processes: megasync 1.1 GB, claude 0.7/0.6/0.6, codex 0.4/0.4/0.3/0.3. findings.title: RETRACTION: E5 Stage-B throughput record is void

findings.detail: stack_numa.py NUMA_NODE0/NUMA_NODE1 are NPS2-era names; on the NPS4 host each cpuset spans TWO nodes (node0=0-23,96-119 node1=24-47,120-143 node2=48-71,144-167 node3=72-95,168-191). frontdoor (8070) and ingest_long_context (8085) launch on them with no numactl policy, so weight pages land on one node at first touch. numactl --interleave binds at FIRST TOUCH only, so it is a no-op on a warm cache - which is why the defect survived casual re-testing. Compounded: llama.cpp mmaps the GGUF, so pages are placed ONCE by whichever instance faults first and every later instance inherits it regardless of its own --membind. Measured 4 quarters at 25.6/25.6/24.2/26.9 pct local under mmap vs 100 pct each under --no-mmap; fleet decode 40.91 -> 52.13 tok/s. Placement therefore depends on instance START ORDER and is nondeterministic across reboots.
findings.title: Root cause: straddling cpusets with no NUMA policy, compounded by shared mmap

findings.detail: llama-bench tg128, spec-dec off, drop_caches per arm, r=5 (frontdoor r=10), kernel v8 binary 10107. As-wired -> canonical (0-95 + interleave=all): frontdoor Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Q8_0 10.83+/-0.04 -> 23.36+/-0.11 (2.16x, LIVE); ingest_long_context Qwen3-Next-80B-Q4_K_M 12.42+/-0.04 -> 22.92+/-0.31 (1.85x, LIVE); worker_general gemma4-26B-Q4_K_M 16.37+/-0.11 -> 39.03+/-0.56 (2.38x, NOT live - already on 0-95+interleave+no_mmap, column A is a counterfactual); architect_general Qwen3.5-122B-Q4_K_M 4.40+/-0.01 -> 11.04+/-0.06 (2.51x, NOT live - already on 0-95+interleave). Only TWO roles are actually losing this. Ratio grows with model size, consistent with a remote-bandwidth mechanism.
findings.title: Measured cost: 2.16x on frontdoor, 1.85x on ingest_long_context

findings.detail: aggregate_predicted_tps was tokens/wall_seconds - not a decode rate (includes load, prefill, idle).
